target_customer: Originally individual consumers and professionals buying NFC business cards; now B2B go-to-market and sales teams capturing leads at in-person events
problem: Paper business cards and trade show leads were slow to share and often never reached a CRM. Popl began as tap to share cards and became an event lead capture platform.
business_model: Hardware sales of NFC cards and devices plus B2B software subscriptions for teams
product_category: Digital business cards and event lead capture

founders.name: Jason Alvarez-Cohen
founders.background_notes: Former Boeing software engineer who learned about NFC at a party in Hollywood per a newsletter profile. Education inferred from the profile saying he was a UCLA fraternity brother of the co-founder; treat as unverified.

founders.name: Nick Eischens
founders.background_notes: Fraternity brother of the CEO at UCLA per a newsletter profile. YC page lists only the CEO.

technical_complexity.rationale: NFC cards with a profile web app were easy to assemble from existing chips and standard app engineering; the later event scanning and enrichment is harder.

defensibility.rationale: NFC card hardware and link pages were commodity, with many rivals selling similar cards, so early advantage came from marketing and brand.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it in the sources found; competition came from startups such as Linq, Blinq and HiHello.

market_need_then: Pandemic era contactless sharing and about 10 billion paper business cards printed yearly were cited as the opportunity; TikTok demand showed consumer pull.

identity.voice_and_tone: Consumer and social first early on, now B2B: Drive growth from in-person.

branding.brand_signature: Tap to share NFC card that went viral on TikTok

rebrands.from: Popl as digital business card company
rebrands.to: Popl as all in one platform for in person lead capture and engagement
rebrands.why: Press release says it moved beyond cards into event lead capture and a universal badge scanner; the name stayed

branding.community_and_virality: A newsletter profile reports over 100 million views and nearly 2 million followers across TikTok, Instagram and Facebook within months, and an ambassador network over 5,000 people.

brand_strength.rationale: A TikTok led launch with large reach and ambassadors drove early growth, but the name is a misspelling of pop that is easy to confuse and no brand merch beyond cards was found.

pivots.from: Digital business cards and NFC devices
pivots.to: Event lead capture with AI badge scanning for B2B teams
pivots.why: Company says B2B event lead capture is the larger opportunity; a third party profile calls B2B the main growth driver

outcome_analysis: Popl grew from TikTok driven sales of NFC cards in 2020 and 2021 into a B2B platform, then rebranded in 2025 around event lead capture. It claims 5,000 plus customer teams and 2 million users. Revenue estimates range from 15M to 34M per data vendors, and public funding appears limited to a small seed, so growth looks capital efficient but unverified.
notes: Funding: aggregators list a seed around March 2021 and totals of 2.2M to 2.7M (CB Insights 2.33M over 3 rounds, with YC and angels such as Sam Altman). No primary or second outlet confirmed, so no round is recorded. Revenue estimates (15M, 34.4M, 10.7M to 32M) are unverified. YC page summary rendered the CEO surname as Alco; other sources say Alvarez-Cohen. Team size conflicts 70 vs 90. Competition list is empty because only undated 2025 and 2026 comparison posts were found. Popl claimed company founded in 2019 by one source and 2020 by another. Completeness pass: the 2021 seed (2.2M per one database, CB Insights dates it 2021-04-06 with total 2.33M over 3 rounds; another source says 2M) rests on databases only; TechCrunch (2021-04-19) confirms YC W21 and Justin Kan backing via Goat Capital but not the amount.
